description: Consent dialog text (core privacy.ts#aiConsentText). Both hosts render these exact words: VS Code calls aiConsentText, Desktop has a Rust port (commands/ai/consent.rs). The policy comes from the cloud preset on the same host. Desktop renders the policyLine cases (the policy URL in the body; its native dialog has no room for a policy button). Regenerate when the copy changes, and update the Rust tables to match.

privacy.leaves: Text you ask about is sent over the internet to the provider and processed on their servers.
privacy.terms: API traffic is covered by the provider's API terms, which differ from its consumer apps. Whether it is retained or used for training is set by those terms and may change; read them before you decide.
privacy.local: A local engine keeps everything on this machine or your network.
privacy.keys: Your API key stays in this app's secure storage on this machine.

sendsText.selection: the selected text and the paragraph before and after it
sendsText.document: the whole document, up to what fits the model
sendsText.documentAndTags: the document, its frontmatter and the tag names used in this workspace

sendsFallback: the text you ask the AI about

policies.label: OpenRouter privacy policy
policies.note: OpenRouter passes each request on to the provider that serves the model, whose own terms apply as well.

policies.label: Gemini API terms and data use

cases.name: rewrite selection, workspace (VS Code: a policy button)

expected.title: Send text to Anthropic?
expected.body:
Anthropic is a cloud engine at api.anthropic.com. If you allow it, this request sends the selected text and the paragraph before and after it. It goes over the internet and is processed on the provider's servers.

API traffic is covered by the provider's API terms, which differ from its consumer apps. Whether it is retained or used for training is set by those terms and may change; read them before you decide.

You can use a local engine instead. Allow for this workspace is remembered; you can change it in AI settings → Cloud consents.
